questions.question: On which date was Haryana formed as a separate state?
questions.rationale: Haryana came into being on 1 November 1966. 18 September 1966 is the date Parliament passed the Punjab Reorganisation Act, the tempting wrong option.

questions.question: Who was the first Chief Minister of Haryana?
questions.rationale: Bhagwat Dayal Sharma took office on 1 November 1966. Rao Birender Singh followed him in March 1967.

questions.question: Which Harappan site in Haryana is regarded as among the largest in the subcontinent and was the subject of a 2019 ancient-DNA study?
questions.rationale: Rakhigarhi (Hisar, now Hansi district) is the large site; Banawali is better known for its fortification and layered phases.

questions.question: The Harappan site of Banawali lies in which district?
questions.rationale: Banawali is in Fatehabad district, excavated by R.S. Bisht of the ASI. Mitathal is in Bhiwani and Farmana is in Rohtak.

questions.question: Which of the following sites is NOT associated with the Indus (Harappan) civilisation in Haryana?
questions.rationale: Thanesar is famous as the capital of Harsha (7th century CE), long after the Harappan period. The other three are Harappan sites.

questions.question: Who ruled from Thanesar before shifting his capital to Kannauj?
questions.rationale: Harsha of the Pushyabhuti dynasty (606-647 CE) ruled from Thanesar and later from Kannauj. The Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang visited during his reign.

questions.question: The First and Second Battles of Tarain were fought in 1191 and 1192. Which statement is correct?
options: Ghori won the first and lost the second
Prithviraj Chauhan won the first and lost the second
questions.rationale: Prithviraj defeated Muhammad Ghori in 1191 but lost to him in 1192. Tarain (Taraori) is in Karnal district.

questions.question: Match the Panipat battle with its year. Which pairing is correct?
questions.rationale: First 1526 (Babur v Ibrahim Lodi), second 1556 (Akbar's forces v Hemu), third 1761 (Abdali v Marathas).

questions.question: Hemu, who briefly held Delhi in 1556, belonged to which present-day Haryana town?
questions.rationale: Hemu spent his early life in Rewari. He took Delhi in October 1556 and was defeated at the Second Battle of Panipat.

questions.question: Who won the Third Battle of Panipat?
questions.rationale: Abdali defeated the Marathas under Sadashivrao Bhau in 1761. Bairam Khan was Akbar's general at the Second Battle.

questions.question: Rao Tula Ram, a leader of the 1857 revolt in Haryana, belonged to which region?
questions.rationale: Rao Tula Ram was of Rewari and led the force that fought at Nasibpur (Narnaul) on 16 November 1857. Nahar Singh ruled Ballabhgarh.

questions.question: Raja Nahar Singh, remembered every 9 January in Haryana, was the ruler of:
questions.rationale: Nahar Singh of Ballabhgarh was hanged at Chandni Chowk, Delhi on 9 January 1858 after supporting Bahadur Shah Zafar.

questions.question: Which commission was set up in 1966 to draw the boundary between Punjabi- and Hindi-speaking areas of Punjab?
questions.rationale: The Shah Commission, headed by Justice J.C. Shah, was constituted in April 1966. Sarkaria looked at Centre-State relations (1983).

questions.question: Which statement about Chandigarh after 1966 is correct?
options: It became the capital of Haryana only
It became part of Himachal Pradesh
It became a Union Territory and a joint capital of Punjab and Haryana
It was handed to Punjab as a district
questions.rationale: Chandigarh was made a Union Territory and the shared capital; the Punjab and Haryana High Court also sits there.

questions.question: Who was the first Governor of Haryana?
questions.rationale: Dharma Vira was Governor from 1 November 1966; Birendra Narayan Chakraborty succeeded him in September 1967.
